_doc: The match racket, an original design: the invented Ostrel Keystone, a pro-style diamond power racket (GDD 2: solid, perforated face, at most 455 mm long and 260 mm wide; GDD 10: rackets of invented designs). Its shape and proportions follow the category's tournament rackets: a broad, rounded top, the widest point high in the head, a full lower head, one open triangular heart between sculpted throat arms, a ribbed collar, a black overgrip and a wrist strap; the graphics and colourway are our own. Metres in the racket's own axes: X across the face, Z along the racket from the butt (-0.075) to the tip, Y through the face, grip centre on the origin (Tools/AssetPipeline/README.md). Read by asset_lib/racket_layout.py, asset_lib/racket_textures.py and blender/build_racket.py; colours are in palette.json 'racket'. See docs/decisions/0008-racket.md.

brand._doc: Invented brand and model, searched before use (no padel brand, racket line or product with either name). The wordmark is drawn from the stroke letters in racket_textures.py, no font files.
brand.name: OSTREL

frame._doc: thickness_m is the regulation maximum of 38 mm. edge_radius_m rounds every edge of the frame, the heart and the throat (Blender curve bevel). The outline is the right half (x >= 0) from the tip down to the neck, in metres, smoothed by a Catmull-Rom spline and mirrored; it is the finished edge, and the builder insets it by edge_radius_m before bevelling. A pro diamond: the top is broad and rounded (about 80 mm across 2 mm below the tip), the widest point is about 60 % of the way up the head, and the lower head stays full before it narrows into the throat. The tip sits bumper.proud_m below 0.38 so that, with the bumper on, the racket is exactly 455 mm long.
frame._face_margin: How far in from the edge the hitting face starts: the frame's own width as seen on the face. No holes in it.
frame._neck: The frame runs on into the handle down to neck_z_m, hidden under the grip, so the grip's finishing tape always covers where they meet.

heart._doc: The open heart: one window, a rounded triangle between the two throat arms. Its top is the bottom of the face, a shallow chevron that dips to top_z_m on the centre line and rises by top_rise towards the arms; its sides follow the arms' inner edges (arm_width_m in from the outline); its bottom closes in a rounded V, notch_m tall, to bottom_z_m on the centre line. Every corner is rounded to about corner_radius_m. bridge_width_m 0 means no bridge (one window); above 0 it splits the window in two and must stay wider than twice frame.edge_radius_m.

holes._doc: Through-holes in the face (regulation diameter 9 to 13 mm). An outer ring that follows the face's own outline, ring_insets_m in from the face edge and spaced pitch_m apart, then a staggered grid (grid_pitch_m, rows from grid_top_z_m down) filling the middle: the dense, even pattern of a tournament racket. Always left-right symmetric, never closer than min_gap_m edge to edge, and none in the wordmark band (keep_clear_z_m) or below it. The emblem is printed and drilled through, like most real face graphics.
holes._lod_segments: Segments per hole at LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2. 0: no geometry; the face material darkens the hole from T_Racket_Masks.A instead, which from the broadcast camera reads the same.

bumper._doc: Matt protector band over the top of the frame, from the tip down to start_deg either side (0 is the tip), proud of the frame by proud_m and wrapping onto the faces by wrap_m. The weight slot is set into it at the tip.

weights._doc: The adjustable-weight look: an alloy weight slot set into the protector at the tip, a rounded slot across the edge with two screws. Cosmetic only: the racket's mass and balance live in Data/ with the shot model.

grip._doc: Elliptical handle under a black perforated overgrip. semi_axes_m is (across X, through Y): about 118 mm round with the overgrip, a mid-size padel grip, and just larger than the frame's neck that runs inside it. The wrap is a helix of overlapping bands (pitch_m apart, raised by step_m at each overlap); the dots of the perforation are printed (T_RacketGrip_Masks). The ribbed collar (collar_ribs rings) closes the top of the wrap over the throat, the flared butt cap the bottom.
grip._lod_segments: Around x along the wrap. LOD0 carries the helix; the lower LODs are plain ellipses.

textures._doc: T_Racket_Masks covers a square of the face, size_m on a side, centred on X = 0 with its top edge at the tip: R emblem (silver), G accent, B ink (the wordmark and the fine print), A holes (so LOD2 shows them without geometry). T_RacketFrame_Masks is the frame's edge unrolled (frame_px, U along the outline from the neck, V across the thickness): the frame lettering in G. T_RacketGrip_Masks is the overgrip unrolled (grip_px, U round, V along the wrap): its perforation dots in G. T_CarbonWeave_Mask is one tile of 2x2 twill carbon, tiled every weave_tile_m (12K-size tows of 5 mm). T_RacketGrit_N is one tile of the raised sand finish that gives the face its grip on the ball (the '3D' texture), tiled every grit_tile_m.

graphics._doc: The original face graphic, in face metres. An arch emblem round the sweet spot: stones voussoirs in silver set in a half ring (inner_r_m to outer_r_m) on piers down to pier_bottom_z_m, its centre stone, the keystone, raised by keystone_lift_m and in the accent colour; the OSTREL wordmark, the model name under it and an accent chevron along the bottom of the face; a short accent line inside the edge on each shoulder (shoulder_z_m); CARBON 18K small at the top. The frame carries OSTREL in the accent colour on each side (frame_text), the grip rows of accent dots. Text heights are cap heights.

strap._doc: The wrist strap: a flat black cord threaded through the butt cap, hanging below it as a narrow loop through a slider. width_m and thickness_m are the cord's; loop_length_m is how far it hangs below the butt, loop_width_m how far apart its two strands are at the bottom. It is not part of the racket's regulation length.
